skill.name: seeker-domains
skill.description: Resolve .skr domains to Solana wallet addresses and find .skr names owned by an address. Integrate lookups into mobile clients or backend services.
skill.summary: Build reliable forward and reverse .skr domain resolution for Solana mobile applications.
skill.author: solana-mobile

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JavaScript template literals, relative imports, named configuration variables, and documentation URLs. The Express reference binds to every interface and omits request throttling, which can expose RPC quota and service availability.

remediation.issue: The Express example listens on every network interface.
remediation.suggestion: Bind local examples to loopback. For public deployments, require an explicit host setting and document firewall, proxy, and access-control requirements.

remediation.issue: RPC-backed lookup routes have no request throttling.
remediation.suggestion: Add per-client rate limits, bounded caching, request timeouts, and provider quota monitoring before presenting the server example as production ready.

content.value_statement: Wallet addresses are difficult to recognize in Solana mobile interfaces. This skill provides tested patterns for resolving .skr names through clients or backend services.
actual_capabilities: Resolve a .skr domain to its current Solana wallet owner.
Find and sort .skr names owned by a wallet address.
Normalize and validate .skr input before making RPC calls.
Integrate lookups through Express routes or direct React Native RPC access.
Display resolved names with a stable truncated-address fallback.
Handle unregistered names separately from RPC service failures.
limitations: Resolution always uses Solana mainnet, even when the application uses another cluster.
Reverse lookup requires getProgramAccounts, which some RPC providers restrict.
The Kit resolver does not return records, avatars, subdomains, or MainDomain selections.
Reverse lookup does not include tokenized domains in its current implementation.

use_cases.title: Add readable wallet labels
use_cases.description: Show .skr names in profiles, friend lists, and transaction history while retaining an address fallback.

use_cases.title: Build a resolution API
use_cases.description: Add validated forward and reverse lookup routes to an existing backend service.

use_cases.title: Prototype direct lookups
use_cases.description: Resolve public .skr data directly in React Native without creating a backend.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve one domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to resolve alice.skr to a Solana wallet address with Solana Kit. Include input validation and not-found handling.

prompt_templates.title: Display a wallet name
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React Native hook that resolves a wallet address to a .skr name. Cache results and fall back to a truncated address.

prompt_templates.title: Add backend routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my existing backend and add forward and reverse .skr resolution routes using its framework conventions. Separate invalid, missing, and RPC failure responses.

prompt_templates.title: Design scalable resolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Design .skr resolution for a high-traffic wallet list. Include batching, caching, rate limits, RPC provider constraints, timeouts, and client fallback behavior.

output_examples.input: Resolve alice.skr and explain each possible result.
output_examples.output: The lookup returns the current owner address, reports that the name is unregistered, or identifies a temporary RPC failure.

output_examples.input: Show a readable label for wallet 5FHw... in a profile.
output_examples.output: The profile displays alice.skr when resolution succeeds and a shortened wallet address when no name is available.

output_examples.input: Plan a backend resolver for a production mobile application.
output: Use mainnet RPC from the server.
Validate domains and addresses before lookup.
Cache stable results and rate-limit public routes.
Return distinct responses for invalid input, missing names, and RPC outages.

best_practices: Keep paid RPC credentials on the server and expose only the resolver API.
Cache successful and missing results because domain ownership changes infrequently.
Preserve a wallet-address fallback so failed resolution never leaves an empty interface.
anti_patterns: Do not place paid RPC keys in EXPO_PUBLIC variables or mobile source code.
Do not treat every RPC error as an unregistered domain.
Do not expose an RPC proxy without rate limits, timeouts, and deployment controls.

faq.question: Which Solana cluster stores .skr domains?
faq.answer: .skr domains are stored on Solana mainnet. Resolve them against mainnet even when the application uses devnet.

faq.question: Can resolution run directly in React Native?
faq.answer: Yes. Direct lookup suits prototypes using a public RPC endpoint, but production applications often need a protected backend and shared cache.

faq.question: Why can reverse lookup fail with some providers?
faq.answer: Reverse lookup uses getProgramAccounts. Some RPC providers disable or rate-limit that method.

faq.question: Does the resolver support names without the .skr suffix?
faq.answer: The Kit resolver accepts either a bare label or a full .skr name. The alternative SDK requires the full domain.

faq.question: Can one wallet own several .skr names?
faq.answer: Yes. Reverse lookup returns a sorted list, and applications can select the first name for stable display.

faq.question: Does this skill resolve avatars and social records?
faq.answer: No. Use an AllDomains SDK when the application needs records, avatars, subdomains, or a selected MainDomain.
